results.title: CTL implication
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For CTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the implication $\varphi \to \psi$ is defined as the disjunction $\neg\varphi \lor \psi$.

results.title: CTL bi-implication
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For CTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the bi-implication $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ is defined as the conjunction $(\varphi \to \psi) \land (\psi \to \varphi)$ of the two implications.

results.title: Exists finally
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ is the existential until $\mathsf{E}[\top \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \varphi]$ with $\top$ on the left.

results.title: The CTL operator $\mathsf{AX}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathsf{AX}\,\varphi$ ("on all next states, $\varphi$") is defined as $\neg\,\mathsf{EX}\,\neg\varphi$.

results.title: The CTL operator AF (inevitably)
results.caption: Definition

results.title: The CTL operator $\mathrm{AG}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathrm{AG}\,\varphi$ is $\neg\,\mathrm{EF}\,\neg\varphi$. It holds at a state exactly when every state reachable from it satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: Existential predecessor operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a labelled transition system and a predicate $Z$ on its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{Pre}_\exists(Z)$ when some successor of $s$ satisfies $Z$: there are a label $a$ and a state $t$ satisfying $Z$ with a transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled $a$.

results.title: Serial transition systems
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A labelled transition system is serial (total) when every state $s$ has a successor: there are a label $a$ and a state $t$ with a transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled $a$.

results.title: Finite runs extend to infinite runs in serial systems
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a serial labelled transition system, if $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ is a finite run of length $k$, then there is an infinite run $s'_0, s'_1, s'_2, \dots$ with $s'_i = s_i$ for every $i \le k$.

results.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ via finite runs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ if and only if there are a sequence of states $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ with $s_0 = s$ and a natural number $k$ such that the sequence is a finite run of length $k$ and $s_k$ satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: One-step expansion of $\mathrm{EU}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be CTL formulas and $s$ a state of a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms. Then $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{E}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathrm{U}} \psi]$ if and only if either $s$ satisfies $\psi$, or $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and some successor of $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{E}[\varphi \mathbin{\mathrm{U}} \psi]$.

results.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ means reachability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ if and only if some state $t$ reachable from $s$ by a finite, possibly empty, sequence of transitions satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: $\mathrm{AG}$ holds iff every reachable state satisfies the formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula and $s$ a state of a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms. Then $s$ satisfies $\mathrm{AG}\,\varphi$ if and only if every state $t$ reachable from $s$ (through a finite sequence of transitions, possibly empty) satisfies $\varphi$.

results.title: $\mathsf{A}(\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi)$ at a deadlocked state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ be a state of a labelled transition system with an atom valuation, and suppose that $s$ is deadlocked: there is no transition from $s$ under any label. Then for all CTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{A}[\varphi\,\mathsf{U}\,\psi]$ if and only if $s$ satisfies $\psi$.

results.title: $\mathrm{AF}$ at a deadlocked state

results.title: One-step expansion of $\mathsf{EF}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$ if and only if $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ or $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EX}\,\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$, that is, some successor of $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EF}\,\varphi$.

results.title: One-step expansion of $\mathsf{EG}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CTL formula. In a labelled transition system with a valuation of the atoms at its states, a state $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$ if and only if $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EX}\,\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$, that is, some successor of $s$ satisfies $\mathsf{EG}\,\varphi$.

results.title: The $\mathsf{EF}$ functional
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a labelled transition system, a valuation of the atoms at its states, and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the map sending a set of states $Z$ to the set of states that satisfy $\varphi$ or have some successor in $Z$.

results.title: The $\mathsf{EF}$ operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a labelled transition system, a valuation of the atoms at its states, and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the monotone operator on sets of states, ordered by inclusion, sending a set $Z$ to the set of states that satisfy $\varphi$ or have some successor in $Z$.

results.title: The functional for $\mathrm{EG}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a labelled transition system, a valuation of the atoms and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the operator that sends a predicate $Z$ on states to the predicate holding at a state $s$ when $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and some successor of $s$ satisfies $Z$, that is, there are a label $a$ and a state $t$ with a transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled $a$ such that $Z$ holds at $t$.

results.title: The $\mathrm{EG}$ functional as a monotone operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a labelled transition system, a valuation of the atoms and a CTL formula $\varphi$, this is the monotone map on predicates on states, ordered pointwise by implication, that sends a predicate $Z$ to the predicate holding at a state $s$ when $s$ satisfies $\varphi$ and some successor of $s$ satisfies $Z$.

results.title: Uniqueness of elementary divisors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be an abelian group. If $A \cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{Z}/p^{e_i}\mathbb{Z}$ and $A \cong \bigoplus_{j=1}^{m} \mathbb{Z}/p^{f_j}\mathbb{Z}$ for positive integers $e_1, \dots, e_n$ and $f_1, \dots, f_m$, then $n = m$ and the multisets $\{e_1, \dots, e_n\}$ and $\{f_1, \dots, f_m\}$ are equal.

results.title: Torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group is finitely generated
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $A$ is a finitely generated abelian group, then its torsion subgroup is finitely generated.

results.title: Torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group is finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $A$ is a finitely generated abelian group, then its torsion subgroup is finite.

results.title: Torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group as a sum of cyclic groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $A$ is a finitely generated abelian group, then there exist a natural number $n$ and positive integers $d_1, \dots, d_n$ such that the torsion subgroup of $A$ is isomorphic to the direct sum $\mathbb{Z}/d_1\mathbb{Z} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathbb{Z}/d_n\mathbb{Z}$ of finite cyclic groups.

results.title: Fundamental theorem of finitely generated abelian groups, invariant factor form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finitely generated abelian group $A$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^a \times \bigoplus_{i < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_i\mathbb{Z}$ for some $a, k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_i > 1$ for every $i$ and $d_i \mid d_j$ whenever $i \le j$.

results.title: Invariant factor decomposition of finite abelian groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite abelian group $A$ is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_i\mathbb{Z}$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_i > 1$ for every $i$ and $d_i \mid d_j$ whenever $i \le j$.

results.title: From elementary divisors to invariant factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $I$ be a finite set, and for each $i \in I$ let $p_i$ be a prime and $e_i$ a natural number. Then there are $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_j > 1$ for every $j$ and $d_j \mid d_l$ whenever $j \le l$, such that $\bigoplus_{i \in I} \mathbb{Z}/p_i^{e_i}\mathbb{Z}$ is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{j < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_j\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Everywhere unramified extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M/F$ be an extension of number fields, with rings of integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ and $\mathcal{O}_M$. Then $M/F$ is everywhere unramified when every prime ideal $\mathfrak{P}$ of $\mathcal{O}_M$ lying over a nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ of $\mathcal{O}_F$ has ramification index $1$ over $\mathcal{O}_F$, and every infinite place of $M$ lying over a real place of $F$ is real.

results.title: Maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a number field, $\overline{F}$ an algebraic closure of $F$, and $p$ a prime. The maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension $F^{\mathrm{un},p}$ of $F$ is the compositum in $\overline{F}$ of all intermediate fields $F \subseteq M \subseteq \overline{F}$ such that $M/F$ is finite, Galois and everywhere unramified, and its Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ is a $p$-group (each such $M$ is a number field).

results.title: Galois group of the maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a number field $F$ and a prime $p$, this is the group $\mathrm{Gal}(F^{\mathrm{un},p}/F)$ of field automorphisms of the maximal unramified pro-$p$ extension $F^{\mathrm{un},p}$ of $F$ that fix $F$, under composition and with the Krull topology.

results.title: Generator rank of a topological group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a topological group $G$, the generator rank $d(G)$ is the least natural number $k$ such that some finite subset $S \subseteq G$ with $k$ elements generates a dense subgroup of $G$. If no finite subset of $G$ generates a dense subgroup, then $d(G) = 0$ by convention.

results.title: Trivial representation on $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$ and a topological group $G$, this is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with the discrete topology, regarded as a continuous representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ on which every element of $G$ acts as the identity.

results.title: Relation rank of a topological group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and a topological group $G$, the relation rank $r(G)$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_p$ of the continuous cohomology group $H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ of degree $2$, with coefficients in the trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{F}_p$. If this space is infinite-dimensional, then $r(G) = 0$ by convention.

results.title: Finite-dimensional second cohomology mod $p$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and a topological group $G$, this is the statement that the continuous cohomology group $H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$ of degree $2$, with coefficients in the trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{F}_p$, is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb{F}_p$.

results.title: Zsigmondy's theorem
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Annihilator of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring, $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ and $G \colon \mathbb{N} \to K$ a sequence, and let $E$ be the translation operator $E(G_s) = G_{s+1}$. The operator $p(E)$ annihilates $G$ when $\sum_i a_i G_{s+i} = 0$ for every $s \ge 0$.

results.title: Every operator annihilates the zero sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every semiring $K$ and every polynomial $p \in K[X]$, the operator $p(E)$ annihilates the zero sequence, where $E$ is the translation operator $E(G_s) = G_{s+1}$.

results.title: The characteristic polynomial annihilates the solutions of its recurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $d \ge 0$ and $a_0, \dots, a_{d-1} \in K$. If a sequence $G \colon \mathbb{N} \to K$ satisfies $G_{n+d} = \sum_{i=0}^{d-1} a_i G_{n+i}$ for every $n \ge 0$, then the characteristic polynomial $X^d - \sum_{i=0}^{d-1} a_i X^i$ of this recurrence annihilates $G$.

results.title: The operator $E - c$ annihilates the powers of $c$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $c \in K$, and let $E$ be the translation operator $E(G_s) = G_{s+1}$ on sequences $G \colon \mathbb{N} \to K$. Then the operator $E - c$, that is, $p(E)$ for the polynomial $p = X - c \in K[X]$, annihilates the sequence $s \mapsto c^s$.

results.title: Comparison test for improper integrals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be interval integrable on $[a, b]$ for every $b \ge a$, with $0 \le f(x) \le g(x)$ for all $x \ge a$. results.title: Limit comparison test for improper integrals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a, L \in \mathbb{R}$ with $L \ne 0$, and let $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be interval integrable on $[a, b]$ for every $b \ge a$, with $f(x) > 0$ and $g(x) > 0$ for all $x \ge a$. If $f(x) / g(x) \to L$ as $x \to \infty$, then $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ converges to a real limit as $b \to \infty$ if and only if $\int_a^b g(x)\,dx$ converges to a real limit as $b \to \infty$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Expressions of the λ-calculus with let
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: An expression is a variable $x$, an application $e_1\,e_2$, an abstraction $\lambda x.\, e$, or a let-binding $\mathsf{let}\ x = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$, where $e$, $e_1$, $e_2$ are expressions and variable names $x$ are strings.

results.title: Monotypes
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A monotype over a set $B$ of base types is a term over the constants $B$: a type variable $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$, a base type $b \in B$, or an arrow $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ of two monotypes (a binary node).

results.title: Type schemes
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A type scheme over base types $B$ is a term over the constant set $B \oplus \mathbb{N}$: its variables $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$ are the free type variables, a constant $\mathrm{inl}\, b$ is the base type $b \in B$, a constant $\mathrm{inr}\, i$ is the bound variable $i$, and a node of two schemes is an arrow.

results.title: Monotypes as type schemes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Every monotype $\tau$ is read as the type scheme with no bound variables of the same shape: a type variable stays the same type variable, a base type $b$ becomes the constant $\mathrm{inl}\, b$, and an arrow $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ becomes the arrow of the images of $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$.

results.title: Evaluation of a type scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given maps $f$ and $g$ from natural numbers to monotypes over $B$, a type scheme $\sigma$ over $B$ evaluates to the monotype obtained by replacing each free type variable $x$ of $\sigma$ by $f(x)$ and each bound variable $i$ by $g(i)$, keeping every base type $b$ unchanged. An arrow $\sigma_1 \to \sigma_2$ evaluates to the arrow from the evaluation of $\sigma_1$ to the evaluation of $\sigma_2$.

results.title: Instantiation of a type scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, the instance of a scheme $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$ is the monotype obtained from $\sigma$ by replacing each bound variable $i$ by $t_i$, keeping its free type variables and base types unchanged.

results.title: Applying a type substitution to a scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type substitution $s$ and a type scheme $\sigma$, $s\sigma$ is the scheme obtained from $\sigma$ by replacing every free type variable $x$ with the monotype $s(x)$, read as a scheme with no bound variables. The bound variables of $\sigma$ are left unchanged.

results.title: Instantiation commutes with substitution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every type substitution $s$, every scheme $\sigma$ and all monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, instantiating each bound variable $i$ of $s(\sigma)$ by $s(t_i)$ gives $s$ applied to the instance of $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$. Here $s$ acts on a scheme through its free type variables only.

results.title: Substitution into a scheme depends only on its free variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two type substitutions $s$ and $t$ satisfy $s(x) = t(x)$ for every free type variable $x$ of a type scheme $\sigma$, then applying $s$ to $\sigma$ gives the same scheme as applying $t$.

results.title: Typing context
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A typing context over base types $B$ is a finite list of bindings $(x, \sigma)$, each pairing a name $x$ (a string) with a type scheme $\sigma$ over $B$. A name may be bound more than once; the first binding of a name in the list is the visible one.

results.title: Context lookup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The lookup of a name $x$ in a typing context $\Gamma$ is the scheme of the first binding of $x$ in $\Gamma$ (the visible one), or nothing if $\Gamma$ has no binding of $x$.

results.title: Free type variables of a name's visible scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a typing context $\Gamma$ and a name $x$, this is the set of free type variables of the scheme that $\Gamma$ binds to $x$ (the first binding of $x$ in $\Gamma$), or the empty set if $\Gamma$ does not bind $x$.

results.title: Free type variables of a context
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The free type variables of a typing context $\Gamma$ are the type variables occurring free in the visible scheme of some name bound in $\Gamma$.

results.title: Free type variables depend only on visible bindings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ give every name $x$ the same visible scheme (or both bind no scheme to $x$), then $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ have the same free type variables.

results.title: Applying a type substitution to a context
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type substitution $s$ and a typing context $\Gamma$, $s\Gamma$ is the context obtained by applying $s$ to the scheme of every binding of $\Gamma$, keeping the names and their order.

results.title: Substitutions agreeing on a context give the same lookups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two type substitutions $s$ and $t$ agree on every free type variable of a context $\Gamma$, then for every name $x$ the lookups of $x$ in $s(\Gamma)$ and in $t(\Gamma)$ are equal: both give no scheme, or both give the same scheme.

results.title: Generalization of a monotype
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a typing context $\Gamma$ and a monotype $\tau$, the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma$ is the type scheme obtained from $\tau$ by turning each type variable $\alpha$ that is not free in $\Gamma$ into the bound variable with index $\alpha$, while type variables free in $\Gamma$ stay free.

results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The syntax-directed Damas–Milner typing relation $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$ between a context $\Gamma$, an expression $e$ and a monotype $\tau$ is the least relation closed under the following rules, where $\Gamma, x : \sigma$ is $\Gamma$ extended by the binding $x : \sigma$ in front.

results.title: More general type scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A scheme $\sigma'$ is more general than a scheme $\sigma$ when every instance of $\sigma$ is also an instance of $\sigma'$ and every free type variable of $\sigma'$ is a free type variable of $\sigma$.

results.title: More general context
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A context $\Gamma'$ is more general than a context $\Gamma$ when the same names are visible in both and, for each such name $x$, the visible scheme of $x$ in $\Gamma'$ is more general than its visible scheme in $\Gamma$. Only lookups matter, so shadowed bindings play no role.

results.title: Contexts with the same lookups are related by generality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ give the same lookup result for every name $x$ (the same visible scheme, or none in both), then $\Gamma'$ is more general than $\Gamma$.

results.title: Extending more general contexts by a binding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ be typing contexts such that $\Gamma'$ is more general than $\Gamma$, let $x$ be a name, and let $\sigma'$ and $\sigma$ be type schemes such that $\sigma'$ is more general than $\sigma$. Then the context obtained by putting the binding $x : \sigma'$ in front of $\Gamma'$ is more general than the context obtained by putting the binding $x : \sigma$ in front of $\Gamma$.

results.title: Generalizing in a context with fewer free variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ be typing contexts such that every free type variable of $\Gamma'$ is a free type variable of $\Gamma$, and let $\tau$ be a monotype. Then the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma'$ is more general than the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma$.

results.title: Typing is preserved in more general contexts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$ and $\Gamma'$ is a context more general than $\Gamma$, then $\Gamma' \vdash e : \tau$.

results.title: Strict upper bound of a finite set of naturals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $S$ of natural numbers, this is the number $\max S + 1$, where the maximum of the empty set is taken to be $0$. It is strictly greater than every element of $S$.

results.title: Hindley–Milner typing is stable under type substitution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $e$ an expression and $\tau$ a monotype with $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$. Then for every type substitution $s$, $s\Gamma \vdash e : s\tau$, where $s\Gamma$ applies $s$ to every scheme of $\Gamma$ and $s\tau$ applies $s$ to $\tau$.

results.title: Typing inversion for variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $x$ a name and $\tau$ a monotype. Then $\Gamma \vdash x : \tau$ holds for the variable expression $x$ if and only if there are a type scheme $\sigma$ and monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that the lookup of $x$ in $\Gamma$ gives $\sigma$ and $\tau$ is the instance of $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$.

results.title: No monotype is an arrow out of itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all monotypes $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$, $\tau_1 \ne (\tau_1 \to \tau_2)$.

results.title: The abstraction $\lambda f.\, f\, f$ has no type
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$, every variable name $f$ and every monotype $\tau$, the judgment $\Gamma \vdash \lambda f.\, f\, f : \tau$ does not hold.

results.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$, all variable names $f$ and $x$, and every type variable $\alpha$, the expression $\mathtt{let}\ f = \lambda x.\, x\ \mathtt{in}\ f\, f$ has type $\alpha \to \alpha$ in $\Gamma$.

results.title: Bound-variable supremum of a type scheme
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bound-variable supremum of a type scheme $\sigma$ is one more than the largest index $i$ of a bound variable occurring in $\sigma$, and $0$ if no bound variable occurs in $\sigma$.

results.title: Type inference for closed expressions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Type inference on an expression $e$ runs Algorithm W on $e$ in the empty context with fresh-variable counter $0$. If W succeeds with a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a counter $n'$, the inferred type of $e$ is $\tau$; if W fails, $e$ has no inferred type.

results.title: Soundness of Algorithm W
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $e$ an expression and $n$ a natural number. If Algorithm W, run on $\Gamma$ and $e$ with fresh-variable counter $n$, succeeds and returns a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a counter $n'$, then $e$ has type $\tau$ in the context $s\Gamma$ obtained by applying $s$ to every type scheme of $\Gamma$.

results.title: Soundness of type inference for closed expressions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every expression $e$ and monotype $\tau$, if type inference for closed expressions returns $\tau$ on $e$, then $e$ has type $\tau$ in the empty context.

results.title: Variables below a bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A term $t$ has all its variables below $n$ when every variable $z$ occurring in $t$ satisfies $z < n$.

results.title: Substituting into a generalization is more general
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a typing context $\Gamma$, a monotype $\tau$ and a type substitution $r$, the scheme obtained by applying $r$ to the free type variables of the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma$ is more general than the generalization of $r(\tau)$ in $r(\Gamma)$: every instance of the latter is an instance of the former, and every free type variable of the former is a free type variable of the latter.

results.title: Generalization depends only on the free variables of the context
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ have the same free type variables, then for every monotype $\tau$ the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma$ equals the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma'$.

results.title: Completeness of type inference for closed expressions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If an expression $e$ has a monotype $\tau'$ in the empty context, then type inference succeeds on $e$ and returns a monotype $\tau$ of which $\tau'$ is a substitution instance: $\tau' = r(\tau)$ for some type substitution $r$.

results.title: Type inference succeeds exactly on typable closed expressions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Type inference succeeds on an expression $e$ if and only if $e$ has some monotype in the empty context.

results.title: Principal types
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inferred type of a closed expression is one of its types, and every type of it is an instance of the inferred one.
